question.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the secant-tangent identity 

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic secant-tangent identity:

$$
1-{tanh}^{2}⁡\theta ={sech}^{2}⁡\theta 
$$

Setting $\theta =4x-1,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}1-{tanh}^{2}⁡(4x-1) & ={sech}^{2}⁡(4x-1).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (5+2{x}^{2}-5{tanh}^{2}⁡(4x-1))\,\text{d}x & =\int (2{x}^{2}+5-5{tanh}^{2}⁡(4x-1))\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int (2{x}^{2}+5[1-{tanh}^{2}⁡(4x-1)])\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int (2{x}^{2}+5{sech}^{2}⁡(4x-1))\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\cdot \frac{{x}^{3}}{3}+5(\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{tanh}⁡(4x-1))+C \\  & =\frac{2{x}^{3}}{3}+\frac{5}{4}\operatorname{tanh}⁡(4x-1)+C.\end{aligned}
$$
